subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration fit (SDK, streaming, embeddings)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: James Miller <james.miller@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration fit (SDK, streaming, embeddings)

James / Samantha —

Thanks again for the 30-min sync today. Pulling the main notes together and next steps so we’re aligned. Happy to hop on a quick follow-up if anything looks off.

Quick recap (high level)
- Pain: Live patient-support assistant latency spikes during concurrent sessions; current costs for embeddings-based reranking are ~2.5x what the team expected for peak workload.
- Goals: Keep sub-300ms median generation latency for triage flows; get embeddings/reranker under a predictable unit cost for 10M monthly queries; structured output (JSON) for downstream analytics.
- Success metrics: 95th percentile latency <= 450ms for the triage path; embeddings cost <= $0.0008 per vector call (target); end-to-end throughput of 40 qps with 200ms queuing SLA.

Product fit points we covered
- SDK changes: You’ll want to use Redwood’s client-side streaming SDK (node/python) to stream partial answers to the UI; we also recommend function-calling hooks for deterministic extraction of structured fields.
- Streaming & structured outputs: Our streaming API supports chunked JSON and incremental function call signals so the UI can render partial results and then reconcile with a final structured payload.
- Embeddings & reranking: For reranking we suggested a hybrid approach: local dense retrieval + Redwood embeddings for re-score; we outlined options to batch embedding requests and use prefix caching to lower per-call cost.

Open questions / risks
- Tokenization differences between your current model and the open model we suggested — we’ll provide a short test harness.
- Endpoint throughput: we should validate peak concurrency with a short load test (we can run this from our Dedicated clusters).

Next steps (owner / ETA)
- Redwood: share lightweight code snippets (streaming SDK + function-calling example) and MUTUAL ACTION PLAN + proposal (attached) — Marissa — by EOD tomorrow (Fri 5/21).
- Acme: share a sample convo dataset (anonymized) and your expected peak concurrency numbers — James / Samantha — by Mon 5/24.
- Technical deep-dive (1 hour) with Acme eng + Redwood infra (Rishi + Vivek) — schedule for week of 5/24.

Attachments: redwood-integration-proposal.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0183

--
Redwood Inference — Production-first inference runtime for developers
From: James Miller <james.miller@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 18:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration fit (SDK, streaming, embeddings)

Thanks Marissa — that’s super helpful. A couple clarifying items from our side: 

1) For the embeddings cost target ($0.0008/vector) — can you confirm whether that assumes batched requests and 8-bit quantization? We currently use a CPU-based embedder for lower throughput but cheaper per-call cost.
2) For streaming: our UI team prefers websocket-style partials (we render tokens as they arrive). Does your streaming SDK support token-level events or only chunk-level JSON?

Samantha and I will pull the anonymized samples and the concurrency numbers — aiming for Mon 5/24.

Also, can Rishi/Vivek join the technical deep-dive? We want to cover model selection and what the fallback behavior looks like during capacity constraints.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—James
James Miller
Director of Product, Acme Health
james.miller@acmehealth.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: James Miller <james.miller@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Redwood integration fit (SDK, streaming, embeddings)

James —

Great questions. Short answers below; Rishi and Vivek can expand in the deep-dive.

- Embeddings cost: The $0.0008 estimate assumes batched embedding calls (batch size 32) and using a quantized model variant on Redwood Dedicated. We’ll include a cost sensitivity table in the proposal (attached).
- Streaming SDK: the Node and Python streaming SDKs support token-level events (on_token) and chunk-level JSON callbacks. For websocket-style partials we have a lightweight example that pipes token events over a websocket; I’ll drop the snippet in the Drive folder.
- Fallback behavior: our smart routing will route to a cheaper compatible model variant when capacity is constrained; we’ll demonstrate this in the test plan (we can show a canary with A/B fallback to ensure quality regressions are visible).

Rishi & Vivek — can you confirm availability for a technical deep-dive next Tue/Wed (5/25-5/26) afternoon PT? We’ll aim for a 60-min slot. Agenda: 1) sample dataset & tokenization check; 2) throughput test plan; 3) SDK integration path + function-calling example; 4) cost/quantization options for embeddings.

James/Samantha — I’ve added a Drive link and the test harness to the shared folder (see link below). If that timeline works we’ll also request an NDA/PO as the next procurement step after the deep-dive.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-acme-integration
HubSpot deal: HS-12537

Thanks — talk soon.

Marissa
